why: Commit 1 rewrites the permission check that builds every role's store menu (canOpen written out in the layout, plus a module-level memo of permissionOfPath()). The equality test only compares storeNav() with storeTabs()/storeAreas() under the same canOpen, so the rewritten canOpen in layout.tsx is held only by two signed-in e2e specs. A key that picked up anything of the member, or an inverted clause, could pass. Commits 2 and 3 are precise: progressTick is pure and tested, the owner-guarded status action is given line by line, and the feed route's UUID branch is still filtered by the account id.
harm_if_wrong: A canOpen or memo that answers for one role with another's result would show menu items to members who may not open them (or hide them from those who may) on every admin screen, and the unit tests would stay green.
make_it_cheaper: Add to commit 1 a unit case that, for each role template in permissions.matrix.test.ts, compares storeNav() built with the new layout canOpen against storeTabs()/storeAreas() built with the old `canOpenPath(holder, p) && (open || keyAllowedWhenNotOpen(permissionOfPath(p)))`, so a wrong rewrite fails without e2e.
brief_problems: The 'under 2 ms' mean timing assertion in a unit test may be flaky on a loaded CI runner; the brief gives no margin or retry.

dreamStateAction is a new exported server action that does not go through storeAction() as CLAUDE.md asks; it follows the file's existing owner() pattern, but the brief does not say this exception is intended.

The int test's Proxy wrapper counts only db().execute; it depends on typedRows() being called with db() as its executor. stop_if covers a 0 count, but the cheap model may not know how to tell whether the wrapper saw the call.
